home-remodeling.local_heading: Two housing markets, one zip code
intro_paragraphs: Hallandale Beach runs two parallel housing markets. East of the Intracoastal, South Ocean Drive is a wall of towers, from the 1960s and 70s buildings around the Hemispheres and Parker Plaza to the newer generation at the Beach Club and 2000 Ocean. West of the bridge sit the low-rise neighborhoods: mid-century houses on the canals of Golden Isles, the condo and townhouse communities off Diana Drive in Three Islands, and the older streets near Atlantic Shores Boulevard. A whole-home remodel here means one of two very different jobs.

Both run through the City of Hallandale Beach Building Division, one of the divisions inside the Department of Sustainable Development, which enforces the Florida Building Code together with Broward's administrative amendments. That second layer is the Broward difference: the county Board of Rules and Appeals interprets the code, hears appeals of building official decisions, and reviews local amendments, so the answer here is not automatically the Miami-Dade answer. Broward sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so impact windows and doors still need HVHZ product approvals. In a tower, the association's approval comes before any of it.

More than twenty years of South Florida construction sit behind PGX Builders Group, along with 150-plus delivered remodels and additions, each one permitted and inspected. In Hallandale Beach that means a fixed written scope before the first wall comes down, a supervisor on site every day, and crews who book the service elevator instead of arguing with the front desk about it. Elevator pads, corridor protection and a clean hallway at five o'clock are part of the job, not a favor. One team carries it from estimate through warranty.
home-remodeling.scope_heading: From concrete out, item by item

scope_items.desc: Windows and sliders carrying HVHZ product approvals, ordered in profiles and colors the association will actually sign off on before fabrication starts.

scope_items.name: Floors that satisfy the board
scope_items.desc: Porcelain, stone or wood installed over acoustic underlayment that meets the sound rating written into your condo documents, specified and documented rather than assumed.

scope_items.name: Millwork and finishes throughout
scope_items.desc: Custom closets, wall panels, doors and casework built to the ceiling heights you actually have, then finished to survive salt air two blocks from the beach.

faqs.q: Who has to approve a full remodel in a Hallandale Beach condo?
faqs.a: Two parties, in order. Your association reviews the plans, the contractor's license and insurance, the work hours and the elevator schedule, and many boards here restrict heavy construction to the off-season. Then the City of Hallandale Beach Building Division reviews for code and issues permits, with inspections along the way. We submit to the board first, because a permit set the association later rejects is a set you paid to draw twice.

faqs.q: What is the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals and why does it matter to me?
faqs.a: It is the county body behind building code administration in Broward: it considers local code amendments, issues formal interpretations when a code section is disputed, and hears appeals of a building official's decision. For you it mostly stays invisible, but it is the reason a detail waved through in Miami-Dade can still draw a comment in Hallandale Beach. Contractors who work both counties without noticing the difference collect rejection letters.

faqs.q: My building is going through its milestone inspection. Should I wait to remodel?
faqs.a: Usually not, but talk to the board first. Milestone inspections and structural integrity reserve studies examine the building's structure and common elements, not your kitchen, and they rarely stop unit work. What they can do is trigger concrete restoration, balcony repairs or a special assessment that competes for the same elevators and the same calendar. We ask the property manager what is scheduled before building a construction sequence around it.

faqs.q: What is a realistic timeline for gutting a whole unit or house?
faqs.a: Design and permitting usually take a few months before anyone swings a hammer, and association review adds its own weeks. Construction on a full-floor condo commonly runs several months; a canal house in Golden Isles with structural work and new openings runs longer. Seasonal restrictions on construction hours can stretch the calendar further. You get a written schedule with the estimate and a supervisor whose job is defending it.

faqs.q: What should a high-end remodel in Hallandale Beach cost?
faqs.a: It depends far more on what is behind the walls than on square footage. A tower unit with original plumbing stacks, no impact glass and a slab that limits where drains can go is a different budget from a recently built residence needing finishes. We price a written specification after walking the space, so the number you sign is the number you pay. We are rarely the cheapest of three bids, and we say so early.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Hallandale Beach Kitchen Remodeling | PGX Builders Group
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Hallandale Beach kitchen remodeling for condos and canal homes: galleys opened, plumbing moved, associations handled. Call (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: A kitchen worth the ocean view
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and real layout changes for Hallandale Beach kitchens, from Golden Isles houses to high-floor units on South Ocean Drive. Permitted, association-coordinated and supervised daily by a licensed general contractor.
intro_paragraphs: The typical Hallandale Beach kitchen was drawn as a closed galley at the back of the unit, facing a service corridor instead of the water. Buildings along South Ocean Drive and the mid-rises on Golden Isles Drive were laid out that way for decades, and so were the mid-century houses in Golden Isles and the townhouses off Layne Boulevard. The remodel almost everyone wants is the same: knock the partition down, put an island where the pass-through was, and let the kitchen see the view the unit was bought for.

Permits come from the Hallandale Beach Building Division, which reviews under the Florida Building Code as amended for Broward, and documents go through the city's online portal rather than by email. In a condo the association reviews first, and its rules usually cover working hours, elevator use, floor sound ratings and who carries the insurance. The physical constraints are the real design driver: plumbing stacks are fixed, the slab decides how far a drain can move, and range hoods can only vent where the building allows.

PGX orders cabinetry early and templates stone after the boxes are set, which is the boring discipline that keeps a kitchen from arriving in the wrong sequence. Slabs come up on a scheduled elevator with pads hung and corridors covered, because your neighbors did not sign up for your renovation. Fixed written scope, a supervisor on site daily, licensed and insured under Lic. CGC1539072, and more than 150 remodels and additions delivered across South Florida, all of them permitted and inspected.

scope_items.name: Lighting worth the view

faqs.q: Can I move the sink and dishwasher in a Hallandale Beach condo?
faqs.a: Within limits. Drain lines need slope, the concrete slab gives you only so much depth, and the vertical stack is not moving, so the further you pull a sink from the stack the harder the geometry gets. Some buildings also restrict coring entirely. We measure the slab, check the riser location and the association's rules, then tell you what the layout can be before a designer draws something the building will never allow.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit just to replace cabinets?
faqs.a: Cabinets alone, no. A real kitchen remodel, yes. The moment you touch plumbing, gas, electrical or a wall, the Hallandale Beach Building Division needs a permit and inspections, and the association will ask for the permit number before releasing the elevator. Unpermitted kitchen work tends to surface at closing, and unwinding it later costs more than doing it correctly the first time. We pull the permits as part of the contract.

faqs.q: Can I get a gas range in a Hallandale Beach tower?
faqs.a: Only if the building already has gas service to the unit, and many here do not. Where there is no gas line, induction has become the honest answer: it delivers the control cooks want and it avoids the venting fight entirely. If your building does have gas, the line still needs a permit and its own inspection. We confirm what is available at the walk-through rather than after the range is ordered.

faqs.q: How do you get stone slabs up to a high floor?
faqs.a: Carefully, and on a booked schedule. Slabs are cut into manageable pieces where the elevator geometry demands it, wrapped, and moved during the hours the association allows, with pads hung and floors protected the whole route. Some buildings restrict deliveries to specific mornings, which is a scheduling problem rather than an obstacle. This gets planned during estimating, not discovered on install day.

faqs.q: What drives the budget on a custom kitchen here?
faqs.a: Cabinetry and stone lead, appliances follow, and the invisible work of relocating plumbing or upgrading electrical is what people forget to price. A galley opened into a great room costs more than a like-for-like replacement, because structure and permits enter the picture. We scope it in writing against a real specification so you are comparing the same kitchen, not three different guesses at one.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Send the floor plan or just open the door. A site visit, a real layout conversation and a fixed written estimate follow, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodels, Hallandale Beach FL | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Bathroom remodeling in Hallandale Beach, FL. Primary suites, frameless glass, flood-tested waterproofing in stacked condo buildings. Call PGX at (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.h1: Bathrooms built for the neighbor below
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless glass and freestanding tubs across Hallandale Beach, with waterproofing flood-tested before tile, permits pulled through the city, and daily supervision from a licensed, insured general contractor.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Waterproofing is a neighbor issue here
intro_paragraphs: Bathrooms date a Hallandale Beach property faster than anything else. Units in the older towers along South Ocean Drive came with a compact primary bath, a tub nobody uses and a vanity built for one person. Houses in Golden Isles and the townhouses in Three Islands tell the same story in a different envelope. What owners build instead is a proper suite: a walk-in shower behind frameless glass, a freestanding tub if the plan earns one, stone rather than cultured marble, and light you can shave by.

The City of Hallandale Beach Building Division permits the work and inspects plumbing, electrical and mechanical before anything gets covered. Condo owners have a second rulebook. Associations here commonly require proof of insurance, a licensed contractor of record, approved work hours and a waterproofing detail they can point to if a claim ever lands. Leaks in a stacked building are not your problem alone, which is why the inspection sequence and a documented flood test are worth more than they cost.

We treat a bathroom as the most failure-prone room in the house, because it is. The waterproofing gets flood-tested and photographed before any tile arrives, slopes are checked with a level, blocking is set before heavy glass is ordered, and the exhaust fan actually terminates outside. Add a fixed written scope, daily supervision and floor protection from the elevator lobby to the work zone. More than two decades of South Florida work, licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072, and every project permitted and inspected.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Every bathroom is scoped to the studs and the slab before selections are locked. These five items carry most of the risk and most of the result.

scope_items.name: Suites carved from small rooms
scope_items.desc: Absorbing a closet or a neighboring hall bath to build a primary suite with room for two people and a door that closes.

scope_items.name: Shower pans that hold
scope_items.desc: Sloped pans, bonded membranes, linear or center drains, and a flood test documented in writing before the first sheet of tile is cut.

scope_items.name: Frameless glass, properly hung
scope_items.desc: Heavy glass panels set on solid blocking and level substrate, because a half-inch of racking in a concrete building shows up immediately.

scope_items.name: Stone, tile and warmth
scope_items.desc: Marble, quartzite and large-format porcelain set over the right underlayment, plus heated floors where the slab and the electrical panel can carry them.

scope_items.name: Ventilation and old piping
scope_items.desc: Replacing tired supply and waste lines while the walls are open, and routing exhaust to a legal termination instead of into a soffit.

faqs.q: Will my condo association let me redo a bathroom?
faqs.a: Almost always, with conditions. Expect to submit plans, your contractor's license and an insurance certificate naming the association, plus a schedule that respects quiet hours and the elevator calendar. Many boards specifically want to see the waterproofing detail, since the unit below is theirs to worry about too. We prepare that submittal package as a matter of course, so approval is a step in the schedule rather than a surprise in it.

faqs.q: Can I have a curbless shower on the tenth floor?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A curbless entry needs recessed depth for the pan, and in a post-tensioned concrete slab you cannot simply cut for it. The workable answers are usually a very low profile curb, a slightly raised floor across the whole bathroom, or a linear drain tight to the wall. We check the structural drawings and the building's coring rules before promising anything, and we would rather say no early than tear out tile later.

faqs.q: How long will I be without the bathroom?
faqs.a: For a single full bath, plan on several weeks of construction once permits are in hand, and add time for custom glass and stone, which are measured after framing and tile are complete. Larger primary suites with structural or plumbing changes run longer. If it is your only bathroom, we phase the work or tell you plainly to plan a stay elsewhere for the rough-in weeks.

faqs.q: The building is doing concrete restoration. Does that affect my bathroom?
faqs.a: It can, mostly through logistics. Restoration projects tie up elevators, staging areas and parking, and they sometimes shut off water risers on short notice. None of that stops a bathroom remodel, but it changes how we sequence rough plumbing and deliveries. We call the property manager before pricing so the construction schedule reflects the building's schedule rather than fighting it.

faqs.q: What separates a high-end bath from a standard one on paper?
faqs.a: Mostly what you cannot see later. Substrate preparation, waterproofing coverage, blocking, tile layout planned so cuts land where they should, and fixtures that hold their finish in salt air. Stone and glass set the visible tone; the plumbing rough sets whether it still looks right in ten years. We put all of it in a written specification, and we compete on that rather than on being the lowest number.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Fifteen minutes on site tells us more than a photo ever will. Written scope and honest numbers follow, in English o en español.

home-additions.meta_description: Golden Isles and Three Islands lots still have room to build. ADUs, second stories and rear extensions in Hallandale Beach. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: Build out, build up, stay put
home-additions.hero_sub: Second stories, rear extensions, garage conversions and accessory suites across Hallandale Beach, engineered, permitted through the city Building Division and built under daily supervision by a licensed general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072.
home-additions.local_heading: Where the square footage actually is
intro_paragraphs: Hallandale Beach is four and a bit square miles with the ocean on one edge and the Miami-Dade line on the other, so almost nobody here is buying more land. The additions get built on the low-rise side of the city: single-story houses in Golden Isles on canal lots, the mid-century streets near Atlantic Shores Boulevard and Foster Road, and the townhouse blocks in Three Islands. The usual requests are a rear family room facing the water, a second floor over a flat-roofed ranch, or a suite for family who now stay all winter.

Additions live or die on zoning before they reach the Building Division. Setbacks, lot coverage and height are checked by the city's Planning and Zoning Division, and overlay districts in parts of Hallandale Beach add their own standards; where a dimension falls short, the city has an administrative variance path that mails notice to property owners within 150 feet and gives them a window to object. The city also adopted an accessory dwelling unit ordinance for single-family properties in 2024, which changed the math on guest suites. On canal lots, flood elevation and federal substantial-improvement limits belong in the first conversation.

An addition is mostly structure, and structure is where a contractor's habits show. Underpinning, new footings, tie-beam upgrades on older block walls and a roof that reads as one roof rather than two are the parts nobody photographs and everybody feels. We seal the construction zone so the rest of the house stays usable, run a fixed written scope with a supervisor on site daily, and keep one accountable team on the job from the first sketch to the warranty call.
home-additions.scope_intro: Every addition starts with a survey, a structural look and a zoning check. These are the projects Hallandale Beach lots most often support.

scope_items.name: Pushing back toward the canal
scope_items.desc: Living space carried toward the canal on new footings, with tie-ins and impact openings drawn into a single permit set instead of three.

scope_items.name: Second floors over block
scope_items.desc: A structural evaluation of the existing walls and footings comes first; the upper floor gets designed to what the building can carry, not what the sketch wants.

scope_items.name: Garages turned into rooms
scope_items.desc: Converting garage and carport space into conditioned living area with insulation, impact windows and mechanical extensions permitted properly, so the added area is legitimate.

scope_items.name: Accessory dwellings and guest suites
scope_items.desc: Detached or attached units for adult children, visiting family or a live-in caregiver, designed to the city's current accessory dwelling rules rather than around them.

scope_items.name: Foundations and flood elevation
scope_items.desc: Footings, columns, tie-beams and, on flood-zone lots, the elevation strategy that keeps the project on the right side of substantial-improvement limits.

faqs.q: Can I add a second story to a Golden Isles house?
faqs.a: Often yes, though the answer comes from a structural engineer rather than a tape measure. The existing block walls and footings get load-checked, and where they come up short the design adds reinforcement, new columns or a heavier tie-beam. Zoning matters just as much, because height and setbacks in Hallandale Beach are checked before anything structural is approved. Sometimes a rear extension buys the same space with less disruption, and we will say so if the numbers point that way.

faqs.q: Are accessory dwelling units really allowed in Hallandale Beach now?
faqs.a: Yes. The city commission adopted an accessory dwelling unit ordinance for single-family properties in April 2024, opening a path that did not exist before: a secondary unit with its own kitchen, bath and sleeping area, attached or detached. The details matter, because size, placement, parking and how the unit relates to the main house are all regulated, and the city records a restrictive covenant against the property. We confirm the current rules against your parcel before drawings begin.

faqs.q: How do flood rules affect an addition on a canal lot?
faqs.a: They set the ceiling on the project. Federal flood rules weigh what you are spending against what the existing structure is worth, and once that ratio is crossed, the whole house has to meet current flood standards, which typically means raising it. Owners along the Golden Isles canals sometimes decide that elevating is the better long-term move anyway. What matters is running the numbers at the concept stage, while the scope can still be steered.

faqs.q: Can we stay in the house while you build the addition?
faqs.a: Usually yes through the structural phase, which is the counterintuitive part. New footings and walls go up outside the existing envelope, so the house stays sealed until we cut through. The disruptive stretch is when the old exterior wall opens and mechanical and electrical get extended. We schedule that window tightly, dust-seal the connection point, and tell you in advance which weeks will be loud.

faqs.q: Does an addition make more sense than moving?
faqs.a: It depends on what you would be replacing. Inventory in Hallandale Beach skews heavily to condominiums, so if you want more house on a canal, there is not an endless supply to shop. An addition lets you keep the lot, the dockage and the street while buying precisely the space you lack. It is also months of permitted construction, which suits owners who intend to stay put. Come to us with the survey and we will tell you honestly whether the lot supports the idea.

home-additions.cta_sub: Bring the survey, the wish list, or just the frustration. Zoning, structure and real numbers get covered on the first visit, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.title: Outdoor Living & Terraces, Hallandale Beach | PGX Builders
outdoor-living.meta_description: Summer kitchens, pergolas, pool decks and driveways in Hallandale Beach, FL. Coastal-grade materials, HVHZ engineering, permits included. Call (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Summer kitchens, pergolas, pool terraces, driveways and exterior renewal for Hallandale Beach homes and canal-front properties, permitted, engineered for coastal wind loads and built by a licensed, insured general contractor.
intro_paragraphs: The good backyards in Hallandale Beach face water. Canal lots in Golden Isles back onto docks and open toward the Intracoastal; houses near Layne Boulevard and Diana Drive look across lakes and waterways; and the properties closest to the beach trade yard space for salt spray. What owners build here is an outdoor room rather than a patio: a covered terrace off the living space, a summer kitchen that gets used year-round, a pool deck that handles wet feet, and a driveway that no longer announces the decade the house was built.

Exterior work brings in more agencies than interior work does. Structures, utilities and paving are permitted through the Hallandale Beach Building Division, with the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals sitting behind that as the county's code authority. Anything at the water line is a separate track: docks, boat lifts and seawalls are licensed through Broward County's Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program alongside the city permit. Pergolas and covered structures need engineered connections, because this is the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone and shade structures fly.

Outdoor work at PGX is built to the same standard as the interior, which mostly means specifying for the environment instead of the photograph. Marine-grade stainless and coated hardware near the water, dense stone sealed correctly, grading and drains sized so a rainstorm ends up in the swale and not against the slab, and every gas, water and power run permitted and inspected. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, tidy sites, and 20-plus years of South Florida construction standing behind the estimate.
outdoor-living.scope_intro: Terraces, kitchens, shade and paving get designed and permitted as one coordinated package instead of five separate trades pointing at each other.

scope_items.name: A summer kitchen with plumbing
scope_items.desc: Outdoor kitchens plumbed, gassed and wired under permit, with stainless rated for coastal exposure and counters that will not chalk out in two seasons.

scope_items.name: Terraces built over concrete
scope_items.desc: Roofed extensions, louvered systems and pergolas with engineered footings and uplift connections detailed for HVHZ wind loads, tied into the existing roof line.

scope_items.name: Pool decks and dock aprons
scope_items.desc: Pavers, shellstone and finished concrete laid with slope and joints planned, including the transition from deck to seawall cap on canal properties.

scope_items.name: Facades and exterior coatings
scope_items.desc: Exterior repair, stucco patching and full recoats, coordinated with re-roofing and window replacement so the building envelope gets fixed once, in the right order.

scope_items.name: Impact doors to the outside
scope_items.desc: Sliders, French doors and folding walls carrying HVHZ approvals, installed so the terrace becomes part of the house instead of a place you visit.

faqs.q: Do I need a county permit for a dock or seawall in Golden Isles?
faqs.a: Typically yes, in addition to the city. Work in, on or under surface waters in Broward, including docks, seawalls, dredging and mangrove trimming, falls under the county's aquatic and wetland resources permitting, and state or federal approvals can also apply depending on scope. The city permits the upland structure. We keep the marine contractor and the terrace work on one schedule so the dock is not finished six months before the deck that reaches it.

faqs.q: Can I build an outdoor kitchen on a condo terrace?
faqs.a: That is an association question first and a code question second. Many buildings prohibit open flame on balconies outright, and even where grills are allowed there are usually restrictions on fuel, fixed installations and anything that penetrates the waterproofing membrane. Ground-floor terraces and private cabana areas have more latitude. We read the condo documents before designing, because a beautiful rendering the board rejects is an expensive drawing.

faqs.q: What materials actually last this close to the ocean?
faqs.a: Salt air is the deciding factor within a few blocks of the beach and along the Intracoastal. Marine-grade stainless, powder-coated aluminum, solid-surface or dense stone counters, and hardware chosen for coastal service will hold up. Standard outdoor cabinets, budget fasteners and thin veneers will not; they rust, streak and fail early. Specifying correctly costs more once and much less over the ten years you own the terrace.

faqs.q: Should the roof and the terrace happen at the same time?
faqs.a: If both are due, yes. Re-roofing, new impact openings, stucco and a covered terrace all touch the same walls and the same waterproofing lines, so doing them together means one round of scaffolding, one set of flashing details and one permit sequence. Splitting them usually means cutting into work you just paid for. We coordinate the roofing trade under the same schedule and the same supervisor.

faqs.q: What moves the price of an outdoor living project?
faqs.a: Structure and utilities, far more than square footage. A paver terrace and a roofed outdoor room with gas, water, power and an appliance package are different projects wearing the same name. Site conditions matter too: drainage, existing slab quality and access for equipment on a narrow canal lot all show up in the number. We walk the property and price a written specification so you are looking at a real scope.

outdoor-living.cta_sub: Walk the property with us, dock and all. Back comes one coordinated plan with permits included and a fixed written price, in English o en español.
